glutamine: L-Glutamine ([watch Dr. Rhonda vid](https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=5DVUEKrekYw&ra=m)) is the main fuel for your enterocytes, and for your immune cells when they're activated. It doesn't have to go through the complicated digestive steps other nutrients do. Inside the mitochondria, it gets turned straight into alpha-ketoglutarate, or α-KG. The α-KG goes into the citric acid cycle, which is how the mitochondria make their energy. So your cells get that energy right away. They use it to repair the gut lining, and that keeps LPS from getting through.
butyrate: Your small intestine runs on glutamine, but the colonocytes lining your large intestine rely on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like butyrate. You get them when your gut bacteria ferment raw resistant starch, or from your home-brewed SIBO yogurt. They feed the colonocytes. They also lock down the barrier in your lower gut, and they keep inflammatory signals turned down across the board.
tca: The TCA cycle is another name for the citric acid cycle, the one glutamine feeds. Organic acids like malic and citric acid are part of that cycle, so they go directly into the same energy pathway in the mitochondria that glutamine does. That means clean sour stuff, like organic malic acid, tart cherries or green apples, gives the cells lining your gut another quick fuel. It speeds up the healing of your gut lining as well, by a different biochemical route than glutamine.
